system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)

- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate

- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer review of Seller update and Disclosure Letter

The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels, market assertions and statement that terms are “FINAL” are not evidence that Wattlebridge agreed them. The recommendations below are buyer opening positions, subject to checking the complete SPA, current diligence and any verified principal-level agreement.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap, preferably **100% of price**, with any negotiated lower general cap confined to general warranty claims. | **Reopen; propose 100%, then negotiate.** A 20% cap transfers substantial undisclosed business risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** individually; only aggregate amounts **above AUD 250,000** are recoverable. | A lower de minimis, aggregation of related claims, and a **tipping basket** under which the whole amount is recoverable once the threshold is crossed; exclude fundamental claims and specific indemnities. | **Reject the excess-only basket.** It leaves the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying loss with the Buyer and can fragment related losses. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months**; limitations are proposed to apply to all claims unless expressly excepted. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with a workable notice procedure and sufficient time after notice to investigate and bring proceedings; separate longer periods for other categories. | **Seek 24 months and express category-specific periods.** An 18-month period may expire before a full annual reporting and audit cycle reveals a problem. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, good title, encumbrances and share capital; **100% price cap**, no general basket or de minimis, and a period aligned with the applicable statutory limitation period. | **Reject the general regime for fundamental claims.** Failure to obtain the shares bargained for warrants materially stronger protection. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to **all claims of any nature**. | An express carve-out preserving all available rights and remedies for fraud, fraudulent concealment and fraudulent misrepresentation, unaffected by caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge or non-reliance clauses, to the extent permitted by law. | **Make this a signing requirement.** The current global wording risks undermining the Buyer’s remedies for deliberate misconduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records; specific disclosures also made. | Disclosure only where **fairly disclosed** against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; identify specific documents or passages and exclude blanket public-record and data-room disclosure. | **Reject blanket disclosure and review each specific disclosure.** Mere presence in a large document set does not necessarily explain the risk or its contractual consequence. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to the Buyer **or advisers**, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete the qualifier; if unavoidable, confine it to **actual knowledge** of named individuals as at signing, without imputed, constructive or adviser knowledge, and preserve specific indemnities and fraud remedies. | **Delete the discoverability standard.** It converts diligence access into a broad waiver even where the Buyer did not identify or understand a problem. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on written consent. No final consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions is included. | A completion condition requiring final written consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer and evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied or effectively waived; no adverse amendments, with a long-stop and termination rights. | **Do not complete on a bare consent alone.** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6m, or 30%, of FY26 revenue, and associated conditions remain unverified. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** facility; release to follow Completion. It remains unpaid and no final discharge is included. | Completion funds flow providing for repayment from Seller proceeds, binding payout figures and discharge undertakings, and simultaneous release or a reliable completion undertaking for all security; reconcile debt-free/cash-free price adjustments. | **Require repayment and secured release mechanics at Completion, not a later promise.** The Buyer should not acquire the company with unaddressed debt or security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | Conditional Completion bonuses of **AUD 420,000** are said to be Seller’s matter but are omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are unknown. | Verify beneficiaries, conditions, timing and on-costs; allocate the economic cost to the Seller through the price adjustment or a specific payment/indemnity mechanism, with no double counting. | **Quantify and expressly allocate bonuses and applicable on-costs.** Completion and continued-employment conditions may affect timing and liability, but omission from funds flow leaves the Buyer exposed. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, without independent verification of non-payment; no receipt or confirmatory assignment is included. | Verify payment directly; require cleared payment and evidence that all SOW3 fees are satisfied, plus a confirmatory assignment or other assurance of rights. Broaden indemnity to associated ownership, infringement, third-party claims and remediation losses, subject to an appropriate separate regime. | **Resolve before Completion and retain a broader indemnity.** Paying a fee alone may not establish clean title or cover the consequences of an IP dispute. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; unauthorised access, exact scope, notification and loss remain unestablished. | Prompt documented investigation and preservation of evidence; assess access, containment, notification and remediation obligations with privacy counsel; obtain a specific indemnity for pre-Completion facts and related costs, with cooperation and conduct provisions. | **Treat as an unresolved risk, not a confirmed breach or quantified loss.** A link went to an unintended external address and up to approximately 1,240 records may be involved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** described as ordinary-course costs, although timing and obligation status are unclear. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together, contracts and renewal deadlines; determine whether each is accrued, unavoidable or terminable, and allocate any pre-Completion or non-ordinary-course exposure through the agreed price mechanics or a specific adjustment. | **Verify before accepting Seller’s characterisation.** The disclosure does not establish whether the costs are ordinary course or economically attributable to the Seller’s period. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise; exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions are similarly broad. | Distinct, expressly drafted regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, purchase-price adjustments and fraud; specify caps, thresholds, periods and permitted remedies for each, including interactions and no double recovery. | **Rewrite the hierarchy and cross-references.** Otherwise a general limitation may unintentionally neutralise a separately negotiated protection. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares and is relied on for title. | Independently verify the register against ASIC and company records, constitution, share issuances and transfers, encumbrances and third-party rights; obtain title warranties and properly executed transfers, releases and completion deliverables. | **Do not rely on the register alone.** It is useful evidence of registered ownership but does not by itself establish unencumbered title or the complete capital position. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | A separate tax covenant or indemnity for pre-Completion tax, with an appropriate longer survival period, cap and exclusions; substantive IP warranties addressing ownership, licences, infringement and protection, plus the specific Ironquay protection. | **Reopen both categories.** General warranty limits and blanket disclosure can leave material historic tax and core SaaS IP exposure inadequately protected. |

**Immediate completion priorities:** obtain the Bluefen consent and evidence of its conditions; agree Riverlark payout and security-release mechanics; resolve Ironquay payment and rights; and quantify the bonuses and incident exposure. The Seller’s disclosure reservations do not resolve those underlying matters.
=== END ADVICE ===
